blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Chelsea in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of extending your Chelsea home? We break down the costs, from $50k for a single room to $150k+ for a full storey, plus tips on Bayside permits.
body: Home extensions are one of the most popular ways to add space and value to a Chelsea property. But understanding the cost can be tricky — especially with Bayside's unique building conditions. In this guide, we'll give you realistic price ranges for 2026, including factors like foundation work on sandy soil and higher material costs near the coast.

A typical single-storey rear extension in Chelsea costs between $50,000 and $100,000 depending on size and finishes. That includes slab, framing, roofing, windows, internal lining and basic fixtures. If you're adding a bathroom or kitchen, expect to add $15,000 to $30,000 for plumbing and tiling. Always budget for an extra 10% contingency.

Two-storey extensions or second-storey additions run from $120,000 to $250,000. These require structural engineering, often steel beams, and careful coordination with existing foundations. Chelsea's sandy soil can mean deeper footings, adding $5,000 to $10,000 to the base cost. A site inspection is essential before quoting.

Council permits for extensions in Kingston and Frankston council areas vary. Expect to pay $1,500 to $3,000 for a building permit, plus additional fees for planning permits if you're extending within a heritage overlay. Donnellan Constructions handles all permit applications as part of our project management service.

Material choices make a big difference. Coastal Chelsea demands salt-resistant materials for external cladding, windows and roofing to avoid corrosion. Fibre cement, Colorbond steel and treated timber are smart choices. They cost slightly more upfront but save thousands in maintenance over the long term.

The timeline for a typical extension in Chelsea is 12 to 18 weeks from start to finish. Delays can happen due to weather (especially in winter) or material shortages. That's why we recommend starting planning in autumn to ensure a smooth build through spring. Our fixed-price contract means no surprises on the final bill.

Financing your extension? Many homeowners use equity from their existing home. Talk to your bank early and get pre-approval before you start. Some builders (including us) offer staged payment plans that align with key milestones — slab, frame, lock-up and completion.

If you're ready to explore an extension for your Chelsea home, call Donnellan Constructions for a free on-site consultation. We'll measure up, discuss your ideas and provide a detailed written quote — no obligation.

blogPosts.title: Coastal Home Building: What You Must Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Building near the coast in Chelsea? Learn about salt exposure, wind loads and the best materials to keep your home looking new for decades.
body: Chelsea's beautiful coastal location comes with unique challenges for builders. Salt-laden air, strong winds and sandy soil all affect how a home is designed and constructed. This guide covers the critical factors every homeowner should know before building or renovating in a Bayside suburb.

Salt exposure is the number one enemy of coastal homes. It corrodes metal fittings, rusts steel frames and degrades paintwork quickly. To combat this, we recommend stainless steel or zinc-alume roofing, aluminium window frames with marine-grade finish, and stainless steel screws and fasteners throughout. These materials cost a bit more but last decades longer.

Wind loads in Chelsea are higher than inland areas because of open bayside exposure. Building codes require specific structural bracing, especially for large windows and roof overhangs. Ceiling battens and roof trusses may need to be engineered to withstand gusts up to 60 km/h. A good builder will factor this into the design from day one.

Sandy soil is common in Chelsea, which can shift or settle over time. Proper foundation design is crucial — typically requiring reinforced concrete slabs with deeper footings than clay soils. Geotechnical testing before construction is a must; it costs around $1,500 but saves huge headaches later.

Another consideration is drainage. Flat blocks near the coast can have poor natural drainage, leading to water pooling around foundations. We always include a perimeter drainage system with gravel and ag-pipe to channel water away from the slab. This prevents damp issues and concrete cancer in the long term.

Choosing the right paint and exterior finishes is also vital. Use high-quality, salt-resistant paint for render and timber. For decks, consider composite decking which won't rot or splinter, or hardwood like Spotted Gum treated with marine oil. Regular maintenance — washing down every six months — will keep everything looking fresh.

The good news is that modern building technology has solutions for every coastal challenge. At Donnellan Constructions, we've been building in Chelsea for over 20 years and know exactly what works. We source local suppliers who understand the coastal environment and provide warranties that stand up to real conditions.

Ready to build your dream coastal home? Get in touch with our team for a free consultation. We'll walk you through every step — from soil testing to final handover — with clear pricing and no hidden costs.

blogPosts.title: The Complete Guide to Renovating a Chelsea Home
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of renovating in Chelsea? From opening up small rooms to adding modern kitchens, here's your step-by-step guide to a successful renovation.
body: Renovating a home in Chelsea can breathe new life into an older property and significantly boost its value. Whether you're updating a 1970s brick veneer or modernising a weatherboard beach house, this guide covers the key steps, costs and local considerations for a successful renovation.

First, define your scope. Common Chelsea renovations include kitchen and bathroom updates, creating open-plan living by removing walls, adding a second bathroom, or re-cladding the exterior. Each has different budget and permit requirements. A full kitchen and bathroom renovation typically costs $40,000 to $70,000, while a cosmetic refresh can be as low as $20,000.

Check your home's structure before you start. Many older Chelsea homes have asbestos in wall linings, floor tiles or roofing. A professional asbestos inspection costs $500 to $1,000, and removal adds $3,000 to $10,000 depending on the amount. Don't skip this step — it's a legal requirement and protects your family's health.

Permits for renovations depend on the work. Replacing kitchen cabinets or flooring usually doesn't need a permit, but moving walls, plumbing or electrical does. If you're altering the building footprint or adding a second storey, you'll need a building permit from Kingston Council. Donnellan Constructions handles all permit applications as part of the project.

Designing for coastal conditions is key. In Chelsea, that means choosing moisture-resistant materials — waterproof gyprock in bathrooms, ceramic or porcelain tiles, and anti-mould paint. Good ventilation, especially in bathrooms and kitchens, prevents mould growth. We recommend installing exhaust fans with humidity sensors for automatic control.

Timing your renovation matters. Spring and autumn are ideal for major work because weather is mild, reducing delays. Winter can slow concrete curing and exterior painting. Summer is fine but can be hot for workers; ensure good ventilation and hydration on site. Plan for 8 to 12 weeks for a full kitchen and bathroom renovation.

Budget wisely. Allocate 15% of your total budget for unexpected issues — rotten timber, outdated wiring, or plumbing problems often surface once walls are opened. Work with a builder who provides a detailed scope of works and a fixed quote, so you know exactly where your money is going. Avoid hourly-rate builders who profit from delays.

Ready to transform your Chelsea home? Contact Donnellan Constructions for a free quote. We'll visit your property, listen to your goals, and provide a fixed-price proposal with a realistic timeline. No obligation, just honest advice.

blogPosts.title: Fixed-Price vs Hourly Rate: Which Builder Pricing is Better?
blogPosts.excerpt: Should you choose a fixed-price contract or an hourly rate for your build? We explain the pros and cons for Chelsea homeowners, with real examples.
body: One of the biggest decisions when hiring a builder is how they charge: fixed-price or hourly rate. Each has advantages, but for most homeowners in Chelsea, fixed-price is the safer choice. This guide breaks down both models so you can make an informed decision for your project.

Fixed-price means the builder quotes a total cost for the entire project, based on detailed plans and specifications. You pay that amount — no more, no less — unless you change the scope. This gives you complete budget certainty. It's ideal for renovations and new homes where the design is finalised before work starts.

Hourly rate (or cost-plus) means you pay for the builder's time and materials as the job progresses, plus a margin. You only pay for what's actually used, which can be cheaper if everything goes smoothly. But if delays or mistakes happen, the cost can blow out significantly. This model suits very small jobs or projects where the scope isn't fixed.

The risks of hourly rate include lack of incentive to finish quickly, and you bear all the cost of unexpected issues. A fixed-price builder has a strong incentive to work efficiently and manage costs because any overrun comes out of their profit. That's why most reputable builders, including Donnellan Constructions, offer fixed-price contracts for renovations and new builds.

However, fixed-price doesn't mean you can change your mind without extra cost. Variations — any change from the original plan — will be quoted separately. That's why it's crucial to finalise your design and selections before signing the contract. Good builders will walk you through every detail to minimise variations.

In Chelsea, we often see homeowners tempted by low hourly rates from unlicensed builders. These rarely end well — poor workmanship, unfinished jobs, and no warranty. Always use a registered building practitioner with insurance. Fixed-price contracts are a sign of a professional, confident builder who stands behind their work.

To get a reliable fixed-price quote, you need a clear scope. That means detailed architectural plans, material selections (tiles, tapware, benchtops) and specifications for fixtures. Donnellan Constructions provides a comprehensive proposal with every item listed, so you know exactly what you're getting. No vague allowances.

If you're planning a build in Chelsea, call us for a free consultation. We'll discuss your project, explain our fixed-price process, and give you a written quote. No lock-in, no pressure — just honest advice from a local team you can trust.
